construct: In low effective circulating volume, renal PGE2 and PGI2 help preserve GFR by dilating the afferent arteriole. NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase and prostaglandin synthesis, removing this compensatory dilation and causing afferent arteriolar constriction, reduced glomerular capillary pressure, and decreased GFR.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Volume depletion plus high-dose NSAID exposure, abrupt creatinine rise, bland urine, and no obstruction indicate NSAID-induced hemodynamic AKI from loss of prostaglandin-dependent afferent dilation.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: NSAID-associated acute interstitial nephritis is the most important competing diagnosis, but an inflammatory interstitial lesion is less consistent with the immediate low-perfusion setting and bland urinalysis.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The combination of volume depletion, temporal NSAID exposure, bland sediment, and no obstruction makes hemodynamic AKI uniquely best.
